mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -1% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day S&P 500 returns observed during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising >= 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.5% monthly change.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 2% in retail sales (RSAFS) and a decline of at least 0.3% in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift from manufacturing to services demand, which historically precedes a mild positive equity market reaction over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +2% AND INDPRO < -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS > +2% and INDPRO < -0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for six consecutive months in an expansionary macro environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports corporate borrowing and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for six consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for six months and UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons for three consecutive months during a period of stable consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% month-over-month) signals weak labor market momentum, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for three months AND CPIAUCSL monthly change < 0.2%
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day S&P 500 returns when PAYEMS < 50,000 for three months and CPIAUCSL change < 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the number of housing units started (HOUST) of at least 1% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts materials and financial sector earnings and correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change >= 1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of HOUST monthly change >= 1%.
